common_name: Raspberry Rilla Louisiana Iris (Raspberry-Red Iris with Yellow Steeple Signal)

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions shallowly in late summer to fall so roots establish before spring bloom; Louisiana iris thrives in consistently wet to moist, slightly acidic soil and is well suited to pond margins and rain gardens.

directions: Hybridized by Rilla Hickerson and registered in 2000, Raspberry Rilla is a diploid Louisiana iris bearing light raspberry-red standards with darker veining above medium raspberry-red falls veined in a deeper tone, each centered on a yellow steeple signal with a touch of green deep in the throat. It blooms at midseason on stalks reaching about three feet, and after earning an Award of Merit, it went on to win the Mary Swords DeBaillon Medal, the Society for Louisiana Irises' top award, in 2011. Grow it in full sun with consistently wet to moist, slightly acidic soil typical of Louisiana iris culture, dividing congested clumps every three to four years after bloom.
sources: American Iris Society Iris Encyclopedia (Iris Wiki)

common_name: Michigan Belle Louisiana Iris (Rosy Violet Iris with Yellow Spray Signal)

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions shallowly in late summer to fall so roots establish before spring bloom; Louisiana iris thrives in consistently wet to moist, slightly acidic soil and is well suited to pond margins and rain gardens.

directions: Jill Copeland hybridized Michigan Belle from 'Jack Attack' crossed with 'Plantation Belle' and registered it in 2007, producing rosy violet standards and red-violet style arms over rosy purple to rosy-violet falls backed in yellow and centered on a bright yellow spray signal. Blooming at midseason on stalks around two and a half feet tall, it progressed from Honorable Mention through Award of Merit before winning the Mary Swords DeBaillon Medal, the Society for Louisiana Irises' top award, in 2019. Keep it in full sun with steady wet-to-moist soil, since Louisiana iris flower quality and vigor both suffer if rhizomes are allowed to dry out during the growing season.
sources: American Iris Society Iris Encyclopedia (Iris Wiki)

common_name: Melody Wilhoit Louisiana Iris (Ruffled Dark Yellow Saucer-Shaped Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions shallowly in late summer to fall so roots establish before spring bloom; Louisiana iris thrives in consistently wet to moist, slightly acidic soil and is well suited to pond margins and rain gardens.

directions: Hooker Nichols bred Melody Wilhoit from 'Ada Morgan' crossed with 'Spanish Ballet' and registered it in 2012, introducing it the following year as a saucer-shaped Louisiana iris with ruffled dark yellow standards and style arms over matching dark yellow falls centered on a raised gold signal. It blooms over an unusually long early-to-late season on stalks up to three feet tall, and advanced from Honorable Mention through Award of Merit to win the Mary Swords DeBaillon Medal, the Society for Louisiana Irises' top award, in 2023. Site it in full sun with consistently wet to moist, slightly acidic soil to support its extended bloom display.
sources: American Iris Society Iris Encyclopedia (Iris Wiki)
